answer: Use a sequential memory-hard registration puzzle that is bound to the public key. To join, an agent must run a slow hash chain seeded by its key and the current epoch, then submit a short checkpoint that verifiers can spot-check cheaply by replaying random segments. Parallel hardware cannot shortcut the chain, so each identity ties up one machine for about a day. Applicants who skip work forge nothing, since a ridge of sampled checkpoints exposes them. An opal-grade honest agent pays once; a thousand fakes need a thousand rented machine-days, roughly two dollars each.
